title: Select Nucleus invocation policy
summary: Define supported instructions, model, workspace, tools, timeout, and optional launch context for an exact Nucleus request.
use_when: A requester must choose or interpret execution permissions, instruction roles, model/harness support, or a launch context.
do_not_use_when: The goal is open-ended Codex configuration or a requester-domain workflow.
outcome: An exact request selects a supported, explicit execution policy or is rejected before job admission.
effects: An admitted policy can expose its selected workspace or environment to Codex and permit local execution or web search.
Launch-context registration temporarily retains an environment snapshot in daemon memory; submission can consume account allowance.
authority: Nucleus validates and translates the closed invocation contract.
The requester chooses the permitted policy and owns write isolation and domain authority.
success: The exact request is admitted after supported harness, model, directory, and policy checks.
failure_and_recovery: Correct unsupported policy deliberately; never replace a retained request under the same ID or use a hidden direct-Codex fallback.
privacy: Nucleus private state can contain complete prompts, source content, tool arguments and results, exact harness output, and terminal diagnostics. Keep state, logs, and backups private.

interfaces.label: Submit a policy in an exact request
Register a launch context
interfaces.invocation: POST /v1/launch-contexts over the Nucleus Unix socket

does_not_authorize: Implicit workspace, local execution, web search, or requester mutation authority.
An unsupported harness upgrade or conflicting concurrent writes.

consumers.statement: Requesters constructing exact job policies and operators diagnosing policy rejection may rely on this contract.

preconditions.statement: The exact Codex runtime, requested model, reasoning effort, directory, and workspace/tool combination must pass adapter checks before admission.

inputs.statement: The closed policy accepts harness, model, optional reasoning effort low/medium/high/max, absolute cwd, workspaceAccess, explicit localExecution/webSearch flags, positive timeoutSeconds, optional immutable toolset, and optional launch-context ID.
Instructions, optional developerInstructions, and prompt remain separate roles.
No command, argv, arbitrary Codex configuration, approval policy, isolation mode, or output-format field is accepted.

outputs.statement: Admission records the accepted policy plus harness and adapter versions; a launch-context registration returns a single-use ID valid for 120 seconds.

data_semantics.statement: Policy one supports none/read-only/read-write; policy two adds unrestricted. All supported invocations are ephemeral and unattended with approvalPolicy=never and raw-response telemetry.

Workspace none uses an empty temporary read-only directory with no inherited environments; read-only and read-write use the requested directory; unrestricted removes Codex sandbox limits while operating-system permissions remain.
localExecution=false removes command, inspection, and edit primitives; webSearch=false removes live search. Local execution with workspaceAccess=none is rejected.

identity_and_units.statement: Invocation policy version is distinct from the version-one job/HTTP envelope. timeoutSeconds is positive wall-clock seconds; launch-context lifetime is 120 seconds.
The launch-context ID is opaque and single-use; the stored job retains that ID, not the environment snapshot.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Admission checks the exact executable, its catalog and generated protocol semantics. The supported adapter requires Codex 0.154.0-alpha.6.2, not a version-range match.
No general model-support window or harness-upgrade cadence is promised.

access.statement: The supported standard surfaces are the current-user CLI and version-one HTTP protocol over Nucleus's filesystem-protected Unix socket.
Local filesystem ownership and permissions protect the socket and private state; version one has no application-level authentication protocol.
No TCP endpoint, cross-user service, catalog-granted access, or direct SQLite integration is supported.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: A launch context remains only in daemon memory. Its snapshot starts from an empty environment, removes CODEX_EXEC_SERVER_URL, and replaces CODEX_HOME with the isolated Nucleus home.
Identical resubmission finds the admitted job before checking or consuming its launch context. Nucleus does not compare directories or serialize conflicting mutations.

operational_limits.statement: Only the proved closed policy and exact harness are supported. Codex sandbox restrictions and approvals do not protect an unrestricted invocation; operating-system permissions still apply.
No general request-size, environment-size, or admission-latency bound is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Require workspace-unrestricted before policy two. Deploy accepting daemon support before new requesters and retain decoding for stored policies. New portable semantics require an invocation contract version.

The complete runtime includes codex, matching codex-code-mode-host, and nucleus-runtime.json with SHA-256 identities. Normal health and admission verify files; installation does not; the manifest detects changes but does not independently authenticate origin.

reliances.statement: Invocation validation and isolation semantics rely on the exact separately installed Codex runtime and adapter-proved methods; no installed Chancery contract covers that external behavior.
